articles.title: Anthropic founder said to plan 'large gift' to Trump Accounts. See who else has pledged.
articles.summary: Over 100 entities have pledged to match donations for Trump Accounts. Experts say it could help reframe the conversation around saving early for children's f...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

In the coming weeks, an Anthropic co-founder will make ‌a "large gift" to ​Trump Accounts. "One of the Anthropic founders is going to make a large gift to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview with ‌CNBC on ⁠Friday.

"We believe that it's important for these great entrepreneurs to share their bounty," Bessent added.

Millions of Trump Accounts, the savings accounts for children, will be funded with an initial $1,000 deposit from the U.S. Treasury. So far, over 100 entities — states, companies, and philanthropists — have pledged to match that seed money with their own donations.

Experts say savings accounts, along with employer contributions, could help reframe the conversation about saving early for children's futures.

While any child under 18 with a Social Security number can establish the IRA-like savings account, only those born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028, get a $1,000 deposit directly from the government as one-time seed money.

Parents and their employers, family members, friends — really anyone — can contribute up to $2,500 per year, beginning on July 5, 2026, with a $5,000 annual cap on contributions .

Charitable organizations and state governments can also make contributions, which do not count against the annual limit. Over 100 states, companies, and philanthropists have pledged to match donations. Below is an updated list. Each company's matching contribution may vary.

Companies pledging matching funds to Trump Accounts

Kraken (accounts for children born in Wyoming in 2026)

Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. and Fox Corp.

Pivot Bio (employee contributions, plus grants to farm customers)

Michael and Susan Dell are providing eligible children aged 10 and under who live in ZIP codes with a median income of $150,000 or less a contribution of $250. The commitment is estimated at $6.25 billion.

Hedge fund founder Ray Dalio and his wife, Barbara, pledged $250 each to about 300,000 children living in Connecticut ZIP codes in households with median incomes below $150,000.

Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner said he would donate $250 to each Indiana child under 5 who has a Trump account.

Rap artist and songwriter Nicki Minaj has pledged $150,000 to $300,000 to the Trump accounts of her fans' children.

Elon Musk said in a post on X on Oct. 19 that next year he will give one SpaceX share to every child in America.

SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband are gifting SpaceX stock to more than 2 million children ages 11 to 17 in lower-income areas.

Ed Freedman's Stable Road Foundation is giving $250 to each Hawaii foster child ages 11 to 17.

An Anthropic co-founder will make a "large gift" to Trump Accounts in the coming weeks, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nov. 20 on CNBC.

Will matching money initiatives for Trump Accounts truly spark American savings?

Lindsey Stanberry, family financial advisor for Babylist.com, an online resource for growing families, says that Trump Accounts may serve as an opportunity to "shift the conversation" in helping families save for their children's futures as early as possible.

She notes that the employer-matching feature works much like a 401(k) plan.

"Adding the cash incentive could encourage more families to prioritize investing in these accounts," Stanberry said. "While the goal of these accounts is to help build wealth for all American children, ultimately, it will be easier for families who have access to employer matching programs."

She hopes to see "a growing wave of corporate participation," and that employers will support both full-time and hourly employees.

Other child savings accounts to consider

IRAs, 529 plans, and education savings accounts are already options for families to consider, in addition to the new Trump Accounts.

"Trump Accounts and 529 accounts are similar in that the money in them can be used to pay for college, but with a Trump Account, your child could also use the money to buy a home, or they could hold on to it to use in retirement," Stanberry noted.

529 accounts have much higher contribution limits, and investment earnings aren't taxed when used to pay for qualified education expenses. Meanwhile, taxes are paid on the investment earnings in Trump Accounts when you withdraw the money, just as with traditional IRAs.

"I think of these like tools in a toolbox, and you don't have to choose just one," Stanberry added. "Families can open a Trump Account to take advantage of the $1,000 seed money and any employer match while also contributing to a 529 to maximize their child's educational funding."

articles.title: IRS releases capital gains tax rates for 2027. See when you'll pay 0%.
articles.summary: Find out what capital gains tax is and how to calculate it. Plus, learn strategies to avoid or reduce your capital gains tax bill.
articles.body:
The IRS has released higher capital gains tax brackets for 2027, increasing the taxable income limits for long-term capital gains, which affect assets held for more than a year. Capital gains tax is a tax on the money you make when you sell an asset for more than you paid for it. Assets can include stocks, bonds, real estate, vehicles, and most other property you own for personal use or as an investment.

How much you owe depends on how long you held the asset and how much taxable income you have. On the flip side, you may be able to deduct some of the losses too.

What is the difference between short-term and long-term capital gains?

There are two types of capital gains: short-term and long-term.

If you own an asset for one year or less, it is short-term, and anything longer than that is long-term. The amount of taxes you may owe depends on how long you have held the asset, which is called the holding period.

The holding period decides which rates apply:

Short-term: You owned the asset for one year or less. The gain is taxed as ordinary income at 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, or 37%.

Long-term: You owned the asset for more than one year. The gain is taxed at 0%, 15%, or 20%.

Holding an asset for more than a year usually lowers your tax bill. To count the holding period, start the day after you acquired the asset and include the day you sold it.

The takeaway for taxpayers: You're likely to owe less in taxes when you hold an asset for the long term.

What are the capital gains tax rates for 2026 and 2027?

Whether you owe taxes on your net capital gain depends on your income level. The more you make in income, the higher the tax rate on your capital gains.

These rates are for taxes due by April 15, 2027 (for assets sold in 2026).

These rates are for taxes due in 2028 (for assets sold in 2027).

Keep in mind, you don't usually owe capital gains taxes if your gain is just on paper. You only have to pay when the gain is realized (when you sell the asset). If you haven't sold it, the gain is unrealized.

You owe taxes when you have a net capital gain. Figuring it out involves some math.

Take your net long-term capital gains for the year and subtract your net short-term capital losses for the year. The result is your net capital gain.

So, if you have $15,000 in net long-term capital gains and $5,000 in net short-term capital losses, you would owe capital gains taxes on $10,000. The amount you'd actually pay depends on your overall income .

What is cost basis, and how do you adjust it?

Basis is what you paid for something, including commissions and fees. You subtract that number from the sale price to find your gain or loss. How you acquired an asset also affects your basis:

Purchased: Your basis is the price you paid (including commissions and fees).

Gifted: Your basis is generally the giver's basis. If the asset was worth less than when you received it and you sell at a loss, the lower market value is used to figure out the loss.

Inherited: Your basis is generally the fair market value on the date of the original owner's death, which is known as a "step-up in basis." Assets that are inherited are also treated generally as long-term, no matter how long you've held them.

Keep in mind that your basis can change over time. Reinvested dividends and, for real estate, major improvements increase it, while depreciation lowers it. Higher basis means a smaller taxable gain, so keep good records.

"A common mistake is either neglecting to factor in cost basis or misreporting it (possibly due to a lack of paperwork to substantiate the basis)," said Garrett Watson, director of Policy Analysis at the Tax Foundation. "[Doing that] could overstate tax liability or, in some cases, understate it if the basis is reported as too high. Getting these details right with thorough documentation is important."

If your capital losses exceed your capital gains, you can use them to lower your income. You can claim the lesser of your total net loss or $3,000 ($1,500 for married filing separately).

If your net capital losses exceed that limit, you might be able to carry the loss forward to later tax years and use it to offset gains in those years.

If you have capital gains or losses to report on your taxes, you will need to fill out a few forms that will go with your Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR.

The first is Form 8949 , Sales and Other Dispositions of Capital Assets. You use this form to gather all the numbers from any 1099-B or 1099-S statements you receive for stock or other market transactions, so you can report those numbers on your Form 1040.

The Form 1099-B is a statement that reports sales from brokerage accounts. The brokerage or financial institution that processed the transaction must send you the form and also send it to the IRS. Form 1099-S is for real estate transactions.

There are two sections: one for short-term gains and another for long-term gains. In both, you'll need a description of what you sold, when you acquired it and sold it, the cost basis, and any adjustments. From that, you'll subtract to get the amount of the gains and losses.

You'll add up all of the gains and losses for a total of both kinds of gains.

Once you have the totals of both short-term and long-term gains, you'll transfer those numbers to Schedule D on the Form 1040.

Again, there are separate sections for reporting short-term and long-term gains, as well as any carryover losses.

At the bottom of the form, you'll do some math and follow other instructions to get the numbers you'll put on the Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR.

The final step is to enter the number you get from this form on line 7 of Form 1040.

Note: Consider consulting with a tax professional, as calculating capital gains taxes can be complex.

Capital gains tax strategies to reduce your bill

Look at the bright side: You made money, even if you have to pay some capital gains taxes. But there are some strategies you can use to reduce those taxes.

Since the tax rate is lower for long-term capital gains than for short-term capital gains, it makes sense to try to hold on to an asset for at least a year.

Put your money in tax-free or tax-deferred investments

You always hear why it's good to invest in a 401(k) or other retirement plan. Here's another one: These accounts grow tax-free or tax-deferred, meaning you don't have to worry about taxes.

"Tax associated with short-term gains and dividends are deferred until withdrawals occur in traditional accounts," Watson from the Tax Foundation explained.

This strategy also includes investments in traditional IRAs, Roth IRAs , 529 savings plans, health savings accounts, and others.

We didn't talk much about capital gains on home sales , but if you keep and use your house as a primary residence for at least two years out of the last five, you may be able to exclude up to $250,000 ($500,000 if married filing jointly) of the gain.

Tax-loss harvesting is a strategy in which you sell an investment at a loss to offset gains from other investments, then reinvest the proceeds into a similar investment.

It's a complex strategy with many rules and regulations about timing, what you can and can't invest in, and more. For example, The IRS wash-sale rule doesn't allow the loss if you buy a substantially idential investment within 30 days befor or after the sale of your asset. It's best to get professional advice because, if done correctly, you can save a lot of money in taxes.

As with many tax concepts, capital gains can be a bit confusing. It's OK to ask for help.

"A tax professional can help determine the proper gross income and cost basis for determining tax owed, which itself can be very helpful and generate tax savings," Watson said.

Another scenario where a professional can help is figuring out the "step-up in basis" rule, "where an asset's cost basis is set at fair market value when it is inherited," Watson explained. "This could still generate a tax bill if there's a realized gain above that fair market value upon sale, but it may be much less than otherwise expected if someone is not familiar with how step-up in basis adjustments work."

A capital gains tax is a tax you pay on the difference between what you paid for an asset and what you made when you sold it.

The length of time you hold the asset determines whether it is a short-term or long-term gain. One year or less is short-term, and longer than a year is long-term.

The tax rates are different for short-term and long-term capital gains and depend on your taxable income. Long-term capital gains are taxed at 0%, 15%, or 20%. Short-term gains are taxed as regular income, at rates of 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, or 37%.

Do I have to pay capital gains taxes immediately?

You pay capital gains tax when you sell the investment (realize the sale).

articles.title: Department-store chain closing half its locations after 188 years in business
articles.summary: David Jones is exiting a market as financial troubles force a major retreat, leaving its future uncertain.
articles.body:
One of the world's oldest department store chains is preparing to shut down half of its physical retail network as mounting financial pressures threaten its future after nearly 188 years.

The major restructuring will affect 19 stores and put approximately 1,500 jobs at risk.

Founded in Sydney, Australia, in 1838, David Jones is a premium department store chain selling luxury and upscale brands across fashion, beauty, homewares, and other categories.

The retailer's latest troubles come after years of financial losses, growing competition, and mounting pressure to restructure its operations.

David Jones is closing half of its store network

David Jones is closing 19 of its 38 stores across Australia and New Zealand, equivalent to half of its physical retail footprint.

New South Wales: 7 Green Hills Hornsby Macarthur Square Macquarie Centre Parramatta Warringah Mall Wollongong Central

Victoria: 3 Glen Waverley Highpoint Malvern Central

Western Australia: 3 Carousel Garden City Hay Street Mall

Queensland: 2 Robina Town Centre Sunshine Plaza

The closures will significantly reduce David Jones' presence in suburban and regional shopping centers, while the retailer also prepares to shut its Hay Street Mall flagship in Perth.

The decision follows a review of the company's store portfolio, with the receiver determining that a smaller physical network is necessary for the business to continue operating.

Most of the affected locations are expected to cease trading by the end of 2026, although the final closure dates have not been confirmed. Until then, the stores will continue trading, with remaining inventory expected to be discounted or transferred to other locations.

The shutdown will leave David Jones without a physical retail presence in New Zealand and significantly reduce its footprint across Australia.

According to the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association (SDA), 1,689 directly employed workers are affected by the closures. Of those, approximately 170 have been offered redeployment, leaving around 1,500 jobs at risk.

"As part of this restructure, the receivers have commenced an immediate consultation process for all staff associated with 19 stores that have been identified for closure," FTI Consulting said, as reported by the Guardian .

"For the immediate term these stores will continue trading and while there is no final date for the closures, we anticipate they will cease trading by the end of the year."

articles.title: Mosca-da-bicheira: praga que devora animais vivos avança nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Casos da Mosca-da-bicheira do Novo Mundo, que devora animais de sangue quente vivos, aumentaram devido ao clima úmido e quente no sudoeste do país.
articles.summary: A mosca-da-bicheira, parasita que devora tecidos vivos, atinge recorde de casos nos EUA e motiva o uso emergencial de insetos estéreis para proteger o rebanho bovino.
articles.body:
Imagem de uma mosca-da-bicheira (Cochliomyia hominivorax). — Foto: Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA.

Os surtos da mosca-da-bicheira do Novo Mundo nos Estados Unidos aumentaram devido ao clima úmido e quente no sudoeste do país, segundo o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA (USDA) e veterinários estaduais. O parasita devora animais de sangue quente vivos e ameaça o rebanho bovino.

A mosca-da-bicheira infestou 64 bovinos, cães, cavalos e outros animais domesticados neste mês, acima dos 34 casos registrados em outubro e dos três em setembro, segundo dados do USDA.

Desde junho, o departamento registrou 149 casos em animais domesticados, além de dois em alces selvagens. Até quinta-feira (26), 73 casos estavam ativos, ante dois no fim de setembro.

Pecuaristas temem que os casos continuem aumentando devido à escassez de moscas estéreis usadas para combater as moscas-da-bicheira.

“O enxame ainda não chegou ao Texas”, disse Susan Storey, uma pecuarista do sul do Texas.

O USDA corre para ampliar a capacidade de produção de moscas estéreis. O Corpo de Engenheiros do Exército supervisiona a construção de uma fábrica no sul do Texas, com inauguração prevista para o próximo ano.

O subsecretário do USDA, Dudley Hoskins, disse à Reuters que está em andamento um projeto para testar moscas estéreis geneticamente modificadas, que poderiam ajudar no combate ao parasita.

O departamento detectou pela primeira vez a mosca-da-bicheira em um bezerro no Texas em junho , após o parasita avançar para o norte através do México. Depois, confirmou mais casos no Texas e no Novo México.

Após um período de calmaria, a mosca-da-bicheira chegou no mês passado ao Arizona, que agora tem nove casos ativos em quatro condados.

As moscas-da-bicheira chegaram ao Arizona pelo sul e pelo leste, segundo o veterinário estadual Ryan Wolker.

“O principal fator contribuinte é a progressão natural da praga e o suprimento limitado de moscas-da-bicheira machos estéreis”, afirmou ele.

O USDA está liberando todas as moscas estéreis disponíveis no sudoeste dos EUA e na região da fronteira norte do México para conter as infestações, enquanto o parasita continua se multiplicando mais ao sul.

Os machos estéreis acasalam com fêmeas selvagens, mas os ovos resultantes desses cruzamentos não eclodem.

“Havia uma boa parte do México onde não tínhamos uma barreira eficaz de moscas estéreis para impedir essa propagação natural”, disse a Dra. Samantha Holeck, veterinária estadual do Novo México. “Agora ela está bem ali na fronteira -- dos dois lados da fronteira.”

Pesquisadores no Panamá avançaram nos testes com moscas estéreis geneticamente modificadas para produzir apenas machos, o que poderia ajudar o USDA no combate às moscas-da-bicheira, segundo Hoskins.

As moscas, conhecidas como NovoFly, poderiam dobrar a produção de insetos estéreis ao eliminar as fêmeas, que não são usadas nos esforços de erradicação , afirmou.

“Até o momento, todos os sinais indicam progresso e uma forte competitividade da NovoFly na natureza”, disse Hoskins. “Os testes realizados até agora demonstraram tudo o que esperávamos que demonstrassem.”

O USDA pretende produzir a NovoFly nas instalações com inauguração prevista para abril no Texas, caso os testes continuem a correr bem, disse Hoskins. Ele acrescentou que levará tempo para aumentar a produção.

articles.title: 'Cobiçadas' por Trump, Filipinas lideram compra de carne suína do Brasil, mas são 22º destino das exportações do agro | G1
articles.standfirst: O presidente dos Estados Unidos afirmou nesta sexta-feira (20) que teria firmado um acordo com o país asiático para assegurar a preferência de produtos agrícolas norte-americanos.
articles.summary: O presidente dos Estados Unidos afirmou nesta sexta-feira (20) que teria firmado um acordo com o país asiático para assegurar a preferência de produtos agrícolas norte-americanos.
articles.body:
A medida poderia reduzir as compras de produtos brasileiros pelas Filipinas, maior cliente da carne suína do Brasil.

As vendas, no entanto, ficarão suspensas por 60 dias a partir de 22 de novembro . A medida vale para vários países e foi adotada após uma investigação do governo filipino apontar que o aumento das importações prejudicou os produtores locais. Segundo o documento, a carne importada chega ao mercado a preços mais baixos do que a produzida no país.

Durante uma entrevista coletiva na Casa Branca, Trump comentou a relação comercial entre Brasil e Filipinas e defendeu a substituição dos produtos brasileiros pelos americanos.

"Eu propus o seguinte: a partir de 1º de janeiro, vocês comprarão 100% de seus produtos agrícolas dos nossos produtores. Nós somos os melhores agricultores do mundo, com os melhores equipamentos do mundo. Vejam bem, nós apoiamos esses países, mas eles não compram de nós. Por isso, eu disse: vocês vão comprar 100% — não 90%, nem 95% — de seus produtos agrícolas de nós. Será que o Brasil vai ajudá-los caso se envolvam em algum pequeno conflito com a China? Duvido muito. Portanto, eles compravam do Brasil e de outros países; agora, passam a comprar 100% de nós — não 99%, mas 100%", disse.

Qual a importância das compras da Filipinas pra o Brasil?

As Filipinas não estão entre os principais compradores dos produtos brasileiros. O país ocupa o 22º lugar no ranking das exportações , com US$ 1,3 bilhão em compras entre janeiro e outubro de 2026, segundo dados do Ministério da Agricultura .

O principal produto vendido pelo Brasil às Filipinas é a carne suína , cujas exportações ultrapassaram US$ 657 milhões no período. Nessa categoria, o país é o principal comprador do produto brasileiro, seguido por Japão e China.

Confira a seguir os outros 5 principais produtos importados pelas Filipinas do Brasil entre janeiro e outubro de 2026:

➡️Carne bovina: com vendas acima de US$ 315 milhões, as Filipinas ocupam o 11º lugar entre os principais compradores do produto brasileiro.

➡️Carne de frango: as importações ultrapassam US$ 181 milhões, colocando as Filipinas na 12ª posição entre os principais compradores do produto brasileiro.

➡️ Álcool: com compras acima de US$ 79 milhões, as Filipinas são o 4º principal comprador do produto brasileiro, atrás da União Europeia (US$ 227,8 milhões), dos Países Baixos (US$ 211,2 milhões) e da Coreia do Sul (US$ 187 milhões).

➡️ Cereais: as exportações brasileiras para as Filipinas alcançaram US$ 63 milhões, sendo quase todo esse valor referente ao milho. Nessa categoria, o país ocupa a 22ª posição entre os compradores do Brasil.

➡️ Fumo: as vendas para as Filipinas ultrapassaram US$ 22 milhões, colocando o país na 22ª posição entre os principais compradores do produto brasileiro.

O Brasil compra poucos produtos das Filipinas. O país representa apenas 0,11% das importações brasileiras , com US$ 18 milhões em vendas. No ranking de fornecedores do Brasil, as Filipinas ocupam o 37º lugar.

Entre os produtos vindos do país asiático estão coco (US$ 8 milhões), gomas, resinas e demais sucos e extratos vegetais (US$ 5 milhões) e óleos vegetais (US$ 1 milhão).

Qual o impacto do embargo à carne suína?

O secretário disse que espera que a suspensão temporária ajude a elevar os preços pagos aos criadores de porcos do país, informou a agência de notícias estatal Philippine News Agency (PNA).

A medida abrange nove categorias de produtos suínos, entre carnes frescas, resfriadas e congeladas e miúdos. Segundo a consultoria Safras & Mercado, essas categorias incluem praticamente toda a carne suína embarcada pelo Brasil às Filipinas, como cortes congelados, cortes com osso e miúdos.

O Ministério da Agricultura afirmou, em nota, que acompanha a implementação da medida e monitora a definição da data de início da restrição, os volumes autorizados e os possíveis impactos sobre as exportações brasileiras.

Segundo a consultoria Safras & Mercado, a carne suína que seria destinada às Filipinas poderá ser redirecionada para outros mercados da Ásia e da América Latina. O aumento da oferta nesses países tende a acirrar a concorrência e pressionar os preços de exportação, principalmente de miúdos e barriga suína.

A restrição também pode ter reflexos no mercado brasileiro. Se os exportadores não encontrarem compradores para esse produto, uma parcela maior da carne permanecerá no país, o que poderá reduzir os preços pagos pelo suíno vivo e pela carcaça no fim do ano, afirma Iglesias .

Vendedor segura peça de carne suína em mercado em Handan, na China — Foto: REUTERS/Stringer

articles.title: Produção mundial de vinho deve ficar perto do menor nível em 65 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: França e Itália foram os países mais atingidos, segundo a Organização Internacional da Vinha e do Vinho (OIV). Brasil, Uruguai e África do Sul tiveram resultados melhores.
articles.summary: França e Itália foram os países mais atingidos, segundo a Organização Internacional da Vinha e do Vinho (OIV). Brasil, Uruguai e África do Sul tiveram resultados melhores.
articles.body:
A produção mundial de vinho deve cair em 2026 e se aproximar do menor nível dos últimos 65 anos, segundo estimativa divulgada na quarta-feira (18) pela Organização Internacional da Vinha e do Vinho (OIV).

O principal motivo, mais uma vez, é o clima: secas e ondas de calor prejudicaram as colheitas de uva em grandes países produtores, como França e Itália, segundo a agência de notícias France-Presse (AFP).

De acordo com a OIV, o mundo deve produzir cerca de 22,5 bilhões de litros de vinho neste ano. O volume é ligeiramente inferior aos 22,7 bilhões de litros registrados em 2025 e está 7% abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos.

Para se ter uma ideia, em 2024, o mundo produziu 22,58 bilhões de litros, o menor volume desde 1961. Isso significa que a produção de 2026 pode ficar até abaixo daquele patamar.

A Europa, responsável pela maior parte da produção mundial de vinho, deve registrar um volume 6% abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos.

França e Itália foram os países mais afetados pela seca e pelas ondas de calor. Na Península Ibérica, Espanha e Portugal também enfrentaram problemas climáticos, embora menos intensos do que em 2025.

Nos Estados Unidos, a produção também deve ficar abaixo da média recente.

No Hemisfério Sul, a produção deve ficar 3% abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos, uma queda menos acentuada do que na Europa. Austrália, Argentina, Chile e Nova Zelândia registraram "colheitas modestas", segundo a OIV.

Brasil, Uruguai e África do Sul tiveram safras maiores, mas esse crescimento não foi suficiente para compensar as perdas dos demais produtores da região.

Segundo a OIV, dois fatores explicam a queda:

Clima: secas e ondas de calor reduzem a produtividade das videiras, ou seja, a quantidade de uva produzida em cada área cultivada;

Redução da área plantada: a superfície destinada ao cultivo de uvas vem diminuindo há anos em vários dos principais países produtores, como a França.

“O aspecto mais marcante deste ano é, assim como nos três anos anteriores, o impacto dos fenômenos climáticos”, disse à AFP o diretor-geral da OIV, John Barker.

“Vivemos quatro anos marcados por eventos climáticos, com repercussões diferentes de acordo com os países. A tendência geral parece indicar que as mudanças climáticas provocam uma maior volatilidade nos volumes de produção”, afirmou.

Segundo Barker, essa instabilidade afeta tanto o Hemisfério Norte quanto o Sul.

articles.title: Builder cancels Bengaluru woman’s Rs 1.65 crore flat despite taking Rs 16.5 lakh payment and allots it to another buyer who paid 50% value; Karnataka RERA orders Rs 5 lakh compensation for mental agony and financial loss even as it hears refund case separately
articles.summary: You book a flat and make part payment for it, and repeatedly follow up for execution of the agreement for sale.
articles.body: You book a flat and make part payment for it, and repeatedly follow up for execution of the agreement for sale. Then you discover that the apartment has been allotted to another buyer. What do you do?A homebuyer who booked an apartment in Bengaluru found herself embroiled in a dispute with the developer after alleging that the flat was allotted to another purchaser without her consent.The Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) has awarded her compensation for the agony. A separate case for refund with interest is pending.What the case is aboutThe dispute concerned a homebuyer who bought an apartment in the developer’s project. The woman buyer booked a three-bedroom apartment, with a carpet area of 1,270 sq ft and one car parking space. The allotment letter was issued in 2024, and the total sale consideration was Rs 1,64,99,147.70, inclusive of applicable GST.The woman’s case was that she had agreed to pay 10% of the sale consideration during booking, followed by 30% in 2025, with the remaining amount payable according to a construction-linked schedule from 2026 onwards.The homebuyer alleged that the Bengaluru developer cancelled her apartment allotment without informing her and allotted the same flat to another purchaser.The woman buyer alleged that she had paid towards the booking, arranged funds for the remaining consideration and repeatedly followed up for execution of the agreement for sale.The order records that the payment schedule had been discussed with the promoter’s representative and approved in writing. The homebuyer stated that she made the booking payment in accordance with this arrangement.In fact, she sold another property in 2025, for Rs 1,02,71,250, according to the sale deed discussed in the order. She said she needed the proceeds to arrange funds for the apartment.A draft agreement for sale was emailed to her on January 23, 2025, but she alleged that the developer failed to complete the formalities despite repeated follow-ups.On February 12, 2025, she was informed that a fresh payment demand of Rs 57.74 lakh had been raised in place of an earlier demand of Rs 35 lakh. On June 28, 2025, she received an email seeking her bank details to process a refund. Agarwal maintained that she had neither requested cancellation of the allotment nor sought a refund.The dispute took a decisive turn on October 30, 2025, when she visited the project site. According to the complaint, she discovered that the apartment had been re-allotted to a third party and that an agreement had been executed with the new purchaser.The order also records that, on November 18, 2025, she was informed that the flat could not be allotted to her because another customer had paid 50% of the consideration.Agarwal sought Rs 15 lakh for mental agony and Rs 25 lakh for financial loss and loss of opportunity. The developer did not appear before the authority despite notice, and the complaint proceeded ex parte.Why did RERA rule in favour of the homebuyer?Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority considered the allotment letter, payment records, email communications and draft agreement.The order noted that the complainant had paid towards the sale consideration but had not received an executed agreement for sale. It also recorded that an agreement concerning the same apartment had been executed in favour of another purchaser.K-RERA treated the developer’s conduct as inconsistent with its contractual commitments and obligations under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. In discussing the absence of an executed agreement despite receipt of payment, the order described this as “a clear violation of RERA Act.”Sunitha Rajesh, Partner at CMS Induslaw tells TOI that the K-RERA order highlights some basic but important principles under the RERA Act.However it is important to note this order is ex-parte i.e., passed without having heard the builder.“The decision was based on one-side of the facts, and the decision may undergo a change in an appeal by the builder,” she says.According to Sunitha Rajesh, the three key facts considered by the authority as are under:First, the builder had collected about Rs 16.5 lakh, which exceeded 10% of the flat's sale consideration of Rs 1.65 crore, without executing an agreement for sale. The RERA Act does not permit a promoter to collect more than 10% of the sale consideration before entering into an agreement for sale.Second, the builder raised demands that were not in accordance with the agreed payment schedule. A payment schedule accepted by both parties cannot be altered unilaterally.Third, the apartment was allotted to another purchaser while the buyer's money continued to remain with the builder. The Authority treated this as a unilateral cancellation by the builder and not as refund.“While awarding compensation, the Authority recognised that when a buyer receives only a refund, the buyer loses not only the money paid but also the opportunity to benefit from the property's appreciation,” Sunitha Rajesh says.“For homebuyers, the case reinforces the importance of ensuring that an agreement for sale is executed before making substantial payments. Buyers should also respond promptly and in writing to any cancellation or refund communication or unilateral changes in the terms agreed at the time of allotment that they do not accept,” she adds.Because this order was passed ex-parte, it may be challenged by the builder and may not be the final word in this matter.In an order dated October 7, 2026, RERA directed the builder to pay the homebuyer Rs 5 lakh towards mental agony, financial loss and loss of opportunity. The developer was also directed to pay Rs 7,000 towards litigation costs.If it failed to comply within 60 days, interest at the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR) plus 2% per annum would apply from the 61st day until realisation.The judgment separately records that the homebuyer had filed another complaint seeking a refund with interest, which was pending adjudication.Thus, the October 7 order did not direct the developer to refund the amount she had paid towards the apartment.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut has created a massive wealth windfall for its founders, employees and early investors, with individual stakes running into billions of dollars. While co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei has an estimated shareholding worth $20.07 billion, other co-founders are not far behind, with each holding equity valued at nearly $20 billion.The Claude chatbot maker made its Wall Street debut on Thursday (local time), with its valuation briefly touching $2 trillion and shares closing nearly 17% higher.Priced at $83 per share, the initial public offering (IPO) has also turned thousands of employees into millionaires on paper, including around 600 whose stock holdings are valued at more than $100 million.The windfall extends to early investors as well. Sound Ventures, founded by actor Ashton Kutcher and entertainment executive Guy Oseary, has valued its stake at $7.5 billion, while investment firm ICONIQ Capital's holding is estimated at $30 billion, Reuters reported.However, these are estimated paper fortunes. The actual wealth that founders, employees and investors can realise remains subject to lock-up periods, vesting conditions and changes in Anthropic's share price.Anthropic co-founders: Who holds how much?The company's seven co-founders have individual stakes valued between $19.76 billion and $20.07 billion, based on the IPO price.Dario Amodei – $20.07 billion: Anthropic's co-founder and chief executive officer.Tom Brown – $20 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Sam McCandlish – $19.92 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Christopher Olah – $19.90 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Jack Clark – $19.83 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Jared Kaplan – $19.83 billion: Co-founder of Anthropic.Daniela Amodei – $19.76 billion: Co-founder, president and board chair of Anthropic.The company's senior management also has substantial holdings. Krishna Rao, Anthropic's chief financial officer, has an estimated stake worth $788.3 million, according to Reuters.Employees: 5,100 millionaires, 600 centi-millionairesAnthropic's IPO has created a remarkable wealth pool among its employees. Around 5,100 staff members, representing 96% of its workforce, now have equity holdings worth more than $1 million.The figures are based on data from Hill.com, which tracks shares in privately held companies. According to regulatory filings, Anthropic had 5,300 employees as of September this year.Around 2,800 employees, known internally as “Ants”, hold shares valued at more than $10 million. Another 600 have crossed the $100 million mark, making them centi-millionaires.Andrew Benson, founder and CEO of Hill, told CNN on Thursday that the speed of wealth creation was particularly striking, especially given how few employees had left the company.“What’s most surprising here is how quickly this this happened,” Benson said.He added, “It’s been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be.”The estimated values of the employees' stakes have been calculated based on a company filing. The figures for the founders, executives and employees are based on estimated holdings at the IPO price.Founded in 2021, Anthropic expanded rapidly from a small artificial intelligence startup to a company employing thousands of people. It had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024, but its workforce had grown to 5,300 by September this year.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Old Monk maker Mohan Meakin, India’s largest rum maker, faces revenue setback after FSSAI questions the composition and labelling of three rum variants produced at its Maharashtra facility; revenue drops 64% in H1 and 77% in the September quarter
articles.summary: India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit.
articles.body: India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit. The company saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year after food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility.The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.The unlisted company’s revenue from operations dropped 64% to Rs 288 crore during April-September, compared with Rs 792 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to its latest financial results. The contraction was even steeper in the September quarter, with revenue falling 77% year-on-year to Rs 108 crore from Rs 473 crore.FSSAI sales restrictions on some Old Monk variantsThe sales restrictions were imposed after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) inspected the company’s manufacturing facility in Khopoli, according to an ET report..The regulator objected to the use of neutral spirit blended with rum flavouring, contending that such products could not be marketed as conventional rum and should instead be classified as rum-flavoured spirits.It also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’. The facility has remained shut since May, according to the financial daily.Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, the company that is responsible for manufacturing and bottling Old Monk in Maharashtra, challenged the FSSAI order before the Bombay High Court.However, it withdrew its petition on November 5, informing the court that it would submit revised labels directly to the regulator for approval. The court disposed of the petition as not pressed, leaving the sales restrictions in place.Mohan Meakin had earlier agreed to drop the claim that the rum had been aged for seven years and make information about the addition of flavouring more prominent on its labels. The regulator, however, maintained that the central dispute concerned how the product itself should be classified.At an October hearing, the company’s lawyers told the court that the restrictions had resulted in losses of around Rs 50 crore for the company and deprived the Maharashtra government of nearly Rs 350 crore in excise revenue. They also said that about 300 workers had been left without work.The regulatory setback comes at a time when Mohan Meakin has been working to restore Old Monk’s market position following years of declining sales, as whisky has gained dominance in India’s liquor market.The brand, which is around seven decades old and has long been associated with winter drinking, hostel rooftops and military canteens, saw its annual sales volume decline to 4.1 million cases in 2013 from a peak of 8 million cases in 2002.Sales subsequently recovered, and two years ago, Old Monk overtook United Spirits’ McDowell’s No. 1 Celebration to become India’s largest-selling rum brand by volume. The brand sold 14 million cases in 2025.The turnaround followed a leadership change after Brigadier Kapil Mohan, the company’s long-serving chairman, died in 2018.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of around $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, placing the five-year-old artificial intelligence company
articles.body: Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of around $2 trillion during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, placing the five-year-old artificial intelligence company among the world's most valuable listed businesses. Its shares later pared their gains, leaving it with a closing fully diluted valuation of about $1.8 trillion, according to Bloomberg.The company’s shares opened at $111.50, around 34% above the initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. They closed at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price, Reuters reported. At the opening price, Anthropic’s fully diluted valuation — calculated using approximately 18 billion shares, including employee stock options and restricted stock units — touched about $2 trillion.Based on its closing price, Bloomberg ranked Anthropic as the world’s seventh most valuable publicly traded company. Six companies were valued higher: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and SpaceX.World's 10 most valuable publicly traded companiesHere's the list of top 10 most valuable publicly traded companies. Figures represent fully diluted market valuations.Apple — $5.1 trillionMicrosoft — $3.7 trillionNvidia — $3.5 trillionAlphabet — $3.3 trillionAmazon — $2.8 trillionSpaceX — $1.9 trillionAnthropic — $1.8 trillionSaudi Aramco — $1.7 trillionBroadcom — $1.7 trillionTaiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) — $1.7 trillionThe listing marks a sharp rise from Anthropic’s valuation of $183 billion around 14 months ago. The company had initially sought a valuation of slightly more than $1 trillion when it began its IPO roadshow earlier in November, according to Reuters.The stock’s early surge was followed by profit-taking, as investors weighed the company’s prospects against concerns over high AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the sector’s long-term profitability."The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, told Reuters."We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability," he added.Led by chief executive Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has positioned itself around AI safety while seeking to build a profitable business despite substantial computing costs. Reuters reported that its revenue rose 47% in the third quarter from the previous quarter, while its net loss narrowed. The company also has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners, including Amazon and Google.Speaking to CNBC on Thursday, Amodei said, "At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future."Anthropic’s performance as a public company will now be watched closely as investors assess its ability to convert rapid revenue growth into sustainable profits and manage its significant computing commitments.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: No invite for China at Anthropic IPO: After SpaceX, Claude parent too shuts Chinese investors out
articles.summary: Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!
articles.body: Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!Earlier billionaire Elon Musk's AI and aerospace giant SpaceX barred investors from Hong Kong and mainland China from buying its shares. Now, Anthropic followed a similar route. While the IPO was open only to investors from selected countries, the repeated exclusion of Chinese investors by major US technology companies raises questions.The artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot reportedly turned away investment from Chinese and Hong Kong firms ahead of its public listing, in what went on to record as the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history.Three people familiar with the decision said Anthropic had excluded investors from the two regions, New York Times reported.The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. As Washington and Beijing compete for supremacy in AI, technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in their already strained relationship.Why keep Chinese investors at arm's length?The exclusion comes against the backdrop of a growing technology rivalry between the US and China. The Trump administration has been taking steps to restrict China's access to advanced AI technology, while both countries are drawing red lines around their homegrown technologies.Anthropic's decision appears in line with a wider trend among major American technology companies. SpaceX and its bankers had taken a similar step ahead of the company's blockbuster IPO in July, shutting Chinese investors out of the offering.OpenAI, another leading AI company, is also expected to bar Chinese investors from its eventual public listing. It has already prevented investors from China from participating in its private fund-raising rounds.There is another common thread connecting all three companies: Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI have all counted the US government among their clients.Trump and Xi may be talking, but technology remains a sticking pointThe decision also comes at an interesting moment in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on Thursday at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China, with both leaders looking to bring some stability and goodwill into an increasingly rocky economic relationship.During the meeting, Xi called on members to build an "open ecosystem" for technology. Yet, while the two leaders are attempting to improve ties, their governments continue to build barriers around trade, technology and capital.The latest developments around AI chips underline just how difficult that balancing act is. Hours before Trump arrived in Asia for meetings with regional leaders, his administration moved to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.Beijing was quick to warn that it could respond with countermeasures if Washington continued with the restrictions."If the US persists, China will take countermeasures," China warned.A spokesman for China's Ministry of Commerce also expressed strong opposition to the latest US measures on Thursday."China is deeply concerned about — and firmly opposes — a series of recent economic and trade restrictive measures taken by the US against China," the spokesman told NYT.The latest restrictions on artificial intelligence are adding to a series of escalating moves by both countries. China experts have warned that the new AI rule could make it harder for Trump and Xi to reach any meaningful agreement to ease tensions.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has acquired a 0.03% stake in US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic for approximately $500
articles.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has acquired a 0.03% stake in US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic for approximately $500 million, following the latter's blockbuster debut on the Nasdaq, according to a report by Focus Taiwan.TSMC's subsidiary, TSMC Partners, purchased 6,024,096 shares in Anthropic at $83 apiece, the same price at which the AI company offered its shares in its initial public offering (IPO). TSMC disclosed the transaction in a filing on Thursday.The purchase was primarily an equity investment, with the payment to be made in a lump sum under Rule 144 of the US Securities Act of 1933, the report said.The investment follows a November 10 decision by TSMC's board to approve investments of up to $500 million each in Anthropic's common shares and preferred shares of OpenAI Group, the company behind ChatGPT.While the latest transaction confirms TSMC's investment in Anthropic, the separate authorisation for OpenAI highlights the chipmaker's interest in two major companies developing artificial intelligence systems.Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, made its Nasdaq debut on November 19 after raising approximately $81.34 billion through its IPO. The offering comprised 980 million shares priced at $83 apiece, making it the largest IPO on record and one of the biggest public listings in the technology sector.The company's shares opened at $111.50, a premium of 34.34% over the IPO price, and climbed to an intraday high of $115.10 before paring gains. They eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.07% from the offering price.At the closing price, Anthropic's fully diluted market valuation stood at $1.76 trillion, after briefly crossing $2 trillion during the opening minutes of trading. Following its much-anticipated market debut, the company's market capitalisation was also reported at approximately $1.44 trillion, against an IPO valuation of around $1.5 trillion.Based in San Francisco, Anthropic trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.TSMC's investment comes at a time when artificial intelligence companies are attracting significant investor capital. Anthropic's strong market debut reflected this interest, with its shares closing well above their IPO price.However, the growing investments in the sector have also come amid concerns over a possible AI bubble, high valuations, rising infrastructure costs and the sustainability of AI-related investments.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, viernes 20 de noviembre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este viernes
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece notablemente este viernes
articles.body: Hoy, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 141,71 €/MWh, lo que representa una diferencia de 109,03 € respecto al precio del día anterior, que fue de 32,68 €/MWh. Este incremento se produce en un viernes, donde los consumidores suelen ajustar sus patrones de consumo. Analizaremos a continuación cuáles son las horas más caras y más baratas del día. La electricidad alcanza sus precios más altos en las horas de mayor demanda, especialmente entre las 18:00 y las 22:00. Durante este periodo, se observa un bloque continuo de horas con tarifas exorbitantes, siendo las más elevadas a las 18:00 (279.32 €/MWh), 19:00 (263.02 €/MWh), 20:00 (259.72 €/MWh) y 21:00 (240.61 €/MWh). Este incremento en el coste refleja una clara tendencia hacia los precios más altos durante las horas pico, donde el consumo se dispara y la oferta se ve limitada. Por lo tanto, los usuarios deben ser conscientes de que las franjas horarias destacadas son: 18:00-21:00 y que los valores clave superan los 250 €/MWh en esos momentos críticos. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro en el consumo de electricidad se concentran durante las primeras horas de la madrugada, donde se registran los precios más bajos. En concreto, las franjas horarias de 01:00 - 02:00 y 02:00 - 03:00 presentan precios de 57.15 €/MWh y 57.36 €/MWh, respectivamente, siendo estas las más destacadas. Durante este período, existe una ventana amplia de precios bajos que se extiende desde la 00:00 - 01:00 hasta poco antes de las 05:00 - 06:00, donde los valores siguen siendo relativamente bajos, pero comienzan a aumentar rápidamente, alcanzando 60.31 €/MWh. En el análisis de las franjas horarias de hoy, se observa una notable concentración de precios elevados a lo largo de la tarde y la noche, alcanzando un pico de 279,32 €/MWh entre las 18:00 y 19:00. Esta tendencia es relevante para el consumidor, ya que resalta la importancia de planificar el consumo de electricidad durante las horas más económicas para maximizar el ahorro.

articles.summary: Stocks are on track to post weekly losses after Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's IPO weren't enough for investors to shake off AI angst.
articles.body: US stocks tanked on Friday as a punishing sell-off deepened after Anthropic's (ANT) successful initial public offering failed to quell broad uncertainty about artificial intelligence safety and financing. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) dropped 1.9% after the blue-chip index fell below 50,000 and neared a correction. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 3.6%. Both the Dow and S&P 500 closed in correction territory, or more than 10% off their peaks. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell nearly 5.3%, with the tech-heavy index closing negative for the year. Investors went risk-off on Friday as semiconductor stocks led an AI trade sell-off. Nvidia (NVDA) shares extended losses, falling 14%. AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), and Micron (MU) stocks also suffered double-digit drops. Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre finds the damage beneath the Nasdaq Composite index is even worse. Seventy-one of the 101 stocks in the narrower Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) were in bear market territory on Friday, including 20 of the 20 semiconductor and memory chip stocks in that index. A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares fell 8%, though they remain narrowly above their IPO price of $83. After a big pop on its IPO day, Anthropic faces a test in the markets to see whether it can sustain the momentum.Other assets slid on Friday as well. Gold futures (GC=F) dropped nearly 4%, while the price of so-called digital gold — bitcoin (BTC-USD) — dropped below $59,000 to trade at its lowest price since July.

articles.title: DGCA issues show-cause notice to SpiceJet over flight cancellations, operational lapses
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking an explanation for rising flight
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking an explanation for rising flight cancellations, operational disruptions and alleged regulatory violations, news agency PTI reported citing sources.In the notice dated November 17, the aviation regulator flagged the airline's deteriorating operational performance, declining on-time performance (OTP), increasing flight delays and cancellations, and failure to adhere to its approved flight schedule.The DGCA also raised concerns over passenger inconvenience caused by disruptions and delays, as well as inadequate passenger facilitation measures. SpiceJet has been directed to respond within seven days of the notice.The regulator said a majority of SpiceJet's aircraft remain grounded and that the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for their return to service."... the majority of the aircraft fleet of SpiceJet is grounded and the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft," the DGCA said.The notice also flagged uncertainty over the renewal of mandatory insurance coverage and concerns raised by overseas aviation authorities over operational disruptions allegedly linked to delayed payments to service providers.The regulator further sought an explanation for SpiceJet's failure to pay a penalty imposed earlier, despite repeated reminders.Violations of international flight norms, route guidelinesThe DGCA said SpiceJet had failed to meet eligibility requirements for scheduled international operations and had repeatedly violated Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG), despite previous enforcement action.The regulator had imposed a penalty on the airline in May for violations, though details of the earlier penalty were not immediately available.The show-cause notice was issued a day before SpiceJet's board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its financial position.SpiceJet's market share falls, shares declineSpiceJet's domestic market share fell to 0.6% in September from 1.2% in August, as the airline continued to face operational challenges resulting in flight delays and cancellations.Its shares fell nearly 5% to Rs 9.74 in afternoon trade on the BSE. The exchange has also sought clarification from the airline regarding reports of the DGCA show-cause notice.The airline's worsening cash crunch has disrupted operations, with several scheduled flights being cancelled amid mounting financial difficulties.Delhi airport warns passengers of flight disruptionsDelhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport has issued an advisory warning passengers that some SpiceJet flights could be affected and asked them to contact the airline for the latest updates."Please note, due to operational challenges being faced by SpiceJet Airlines, some flights may be impacted. Passengers are requested to contact SpiceJet directly for the latest information regarding their flight status and travel plans. Thank you for your patience and understanding," the airport said.The advisory comes as SpiceJet struggles with mounting flight cancellations and financial woes.Despite receiving DGCA approval to operate around 66 flights daily under the winter schedule, the airline has reportedly been operating barely 15 flights a day while continuing to accept bookings across its published schedule, according to an ET report.For the second consecutive day on Friday, Delhi airport operator DIAL issued a similar advisory on X, warning passengers that some flights could be affected due to operational challenges faced by SpiceJet.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: What's next for Anthropic shares - will it boom or pop?
articles.summary: Anthropic's record-breaking stock market debut has put the artificial intelligence company at the centre of a new debate over whether the AI boom can
articles.body: Anthropic's record-breaking stock market debut has put the artificial intelligence company at the centre of a new debate over whether the AI boom can sustain its momentum. The maker of Claude chatbot ended its first day of trading on Thursday with a market valuation of around $1.75 trillion, after raising $81 billion in what was reported as the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history. But concerns over the industry's high spending, mounting risks and market volatility have raised questions about what lies ahead for its shares.The stock surged as much as 34% after trading began before closing about 17% above its IPO price at just over $97. The debut has made Anthropic one of the world's most valuable companies, but investors will now be watching whether the rally holds and how the company manages its growing costs, infrastructure investments and safety commitments.Why the AI market remains under pressureAnthropic's debut comes at a time when investor confidence in the broader AI industry remains unsettled. Major US stock indexes fell to seven-month lows on Thursday, while Asian markets also saw sharp declines in early trading on Friday.Despite the strong demand for Anthropic shares, analysts say its debut alone may not be enough to reassure investors about the long-term outlook for AI companies.Revenue is soaring, but so are costsAnthropic's rapid growth has been reflected in its revenue. According to its investor prospectus, the company generated $16.2 billion in revenue in the first six months of 2026, compared with $4.6 billion for the whole of 2025.However, the company has also reported substantial losses, including a reported $80 billion loss in the first half of 2026, largely attributed to a one-off charge. Its losses reportedly reached $104 billion in the first nine months of 2026.Anthropic is expected to spend heavily on infrastructure as it expands its AI operations. The company has plans to spend around $900 billion on data centre infrastructure over the next two decades, raising concerns about the scale of capital it may need to sustain its growth.The IPO provides the company with fresh capital for these investments, but analysts expect spending requirements and financing needs to remain a key concern for investors.Data centres and regulation could weigh on sharesAnthropic's expansion also comes amid growing opposition to AI infrastructure, particularly data centres, in the US. Protests against proposed data centre projects have gained momentum, with some municipalities and states voting for restrictions or bans.The company's growth is closely tied to investments in the infrastructure that powers AI tools such as Claude. A slowdown in data centre spending could have implications not just for Anthropic but also for the wider US economy.Regulatory scrutiny is another factor investors will be watching. Senior Democrats have signalled the possibility of tighter oversight of AI companies, citing concerns over the risks posed by advanced AI systems and the volatility that large AI IPOs could introduce into financial markets.Last month, Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, warning that the company's IPO “could inject extreme volatility and risk into the financial system, which threatens to undermine Americans' economic security.”Anthropic's safety pledge faces scrutinyAnthropic was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including CEO Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is the company's president. The founders left OpenAI with a focus on prioritising safety in AI development.The company has repeatedly warned about the potential risks of advanced AI, even as it continues to develop increasingly powerful models. In a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic devoted 93 pages to risk factors, including the possibility that advanced AI systems could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.”However, the company's safety commitments have also come under scrutiny. Researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, criticising the safety practices of both Anthropic and OpenAI and arguing that the industry was moving too quickly.Amodei has called for a slowdown in AI development and advocated greater coordination between companies and countries, along with independent evaluations of AI systems.Speaking at the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday, Amodei said the company's “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us”.“And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” he said.The tension between Anthropic's safety commitments and its commercial ambitions is likely to remain a key issue as the company enters public markets.What's next for Anthropic?Anthropic's performance in the coming months will depend on whether it can sustain its growth while managing rising infrastructure costs, regulatory scrutiny and concerns over the risks of advanced AI. The company's expansion is also tied to data centre investments, which have faced growing opposition in the US, with some municipalities and states voting for restrictions or bans.Regulatory oversight could add another layer of uncertainty. Senior Democrats have signalled the possibility of tighter scrutiny of AI companies over the risks posed by advanced AI systems and the volatility large IPOs could introduce into financial markets.Anthropic's safety commitments are also likely to remain under scrutiny. The company has repeatedly warned about the risks of advanced AI even as it continues to develop increasingly powerful models. CEO Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday that the company's “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us”.The debut could also offer a signal for other AI firms planning to enter public markets. OpenAI, Anthropic's major rival, is expected to pursue an IPO in 2027. CEO Sam Altman said earlier this week that the company would go ahead with its IPO next year despite market volatility, adding, “There's been way too much investor demand and not enough supply.”Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Bending Spoons to buy Mailchimp from Intuit in $3.68B deal
articles.summary: The Italian tech company behind WeTransfer and Vimeo has agreed to buy email marketing platform Mailchimp. Intuit is selling it for less than a third of what...
articles.body:
The Italian company Bending Spoons agreed on Thursday to buy Mailchimp, the US email marketing platform, from Intuit ( INTU ) for $3.68 billion (€3.35bn).

Intuit bought Mailchimp in 2021 for around $12bn (€10.9bn at the 19 November exchange rate).

Under the agreement, Intuit will reinvest $368 million (€335mn) of its proceeds in new Bending Spoons shares, according to the Italian company.

Intuit's shares fell almost 8% before the bell on Friday.

Mailchimp's quarterly revenue fell 1% to $313mn (€285mn), Intuit said. The US company said the sale would help it focus on AI-powered tools for businesses.

The company's co-founder and chief executive Luca Ferrari described Mailchimp as "a prestigious brand which in more than twenty years has revolutionised the email marketing sector, redefining the way companies grow their audiences".

He said Bending Spoons ( BSP ) planned to invest heavily in the business and build on the tools its customers already use.

Intuit's board approved the deal, which still needs regulatory approval and is expected to close in early 2027.

Under the agreement, Bending Spoons will buy all of The Rocket Science Group LLC, the company behind Mailchimp, along with other Mailchimp assets and liabilities.

How Bending Spoons grew through acquisitions

Founded in 2013 in Copenhagen and now based in Milan, Bending Spoons has grown by acquiring other companies in the web services sector, then improving and relaunching their products. It has been listed on Nasdaq since 1 July 2026, with an IPO price of $29 a share.

The company started out designing, developing and maintaining software. It has since made more than 50 acquisitions, including WeTransfer in 2024, Vimeo in 2025 and Eventbrite and Airtable in 2026. It often buys products it sees as underperforming and invests in improving them.

The company has also been described as a "unicorn", a term generally used for a privately held start-up valued at more than $1bn (€910mn). In a 2024 LinkedIn post, Roma Startup president Gianmarco Carnovale argued that the label did not fit Bending Spoons because of how it started.

In Italy, the firm is also known for developing the Immuni app, which the Italian government promoted during the Covid-19 pandemic and which struggled to gain traction. Immuni and Live Quiz are examples of apps Bending Spoons developed from scratch.

articles.title: Delhi woman loses Rs 77,114 in unauthorised transactions after issues with her mobile phone delay SMS alerts, she alerts bank but gets no refund; consumer commission orders bank to pay Rs 70,084 with 7% interest and Rs 25,000 as compensation and litigation expenses
articles.summary: What happens if you lose money from your bank account due to unauthorised transactions? Is the bank liable to pay you?
articles.body: What happens if you lose money from your bank account due to unauthorised transactions? Is the bank liable to pay you? In one such case a Delhi-based woman took her bank to court after losing money in three online transactions in 2016 that she said she had not authorised.Accusing her of deficiency in service, the woman sought a refund of Rs 2,28,839, along with 18% interest, ECS charges, revival penalties, compensation for mental agony and Rs 25,000 towards litigation expenses.The bank, however, maintained that customers were responsible for any leakage of their one-time passwords (OTPs) and card details. The Delhi Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ultimately ruled in the woman’s favour.What the case is aboutThe woman claimed that three unauthorised online transactions, carried out on July 4, July 5 and July 9, 2016, resulted in a total of Rs 77,114 being deducted from her bank account.She said she was experiencing problems with her mobile phone during that period and was consequently unable to access the internet. She also alleged that no SMS alerts were received when the transactions took place.According to Varsha, she received a delayed SMS notification on July 10, 2017, following which she immediately approached her bank and requested that all transactions in her account be blocked. She also filed a police complaint at the police station.The woman further alleged that the unauthorised debits led to ECS penalty charges being imposed by the bank and affected her mutual fund investments. She also said her life insurance policy lapsed and had to be revived after she paid the applicable penalty charges.As the bank did not return the money lost in the disputed transactions, the woman sent it a legal notice dated May 2, 2018.In its response before the commission, the bank said it “is not responsible for transfer of funds to any third party.According to an ET report on the judgement, the bank also argued that the account holder had not received the OTPs because her mobile phone was not working. “The leakage of OTP and the card details is the responsibility of the card holder,” it stated, seeking dismissal of the complaint.Why did the Consumer Commission rule in favour of the bank account holder?The Consumer Commission referred to an email sent by the woman on 10 July 2016, in which she had provided details of the fraudulent transactions carried out on July 4, 5 and 9.The email stated: “Rs 5,000 was used for unauthorised transaction on 04.07.2016, Rs 2,000 on 05.07.2016 and Rs 70,084 on 09.07.2016.”The commission also relied on the RBI circular titled ‘Customer Protection-Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorized Electronic Banking Transaction’. The circular provides for zero liability for customers when an unauthorised transaction occurs due to fraud, negligence or deficiency on the bank’s part, or because of a breach by a third party.After a legal battle lasting nearly a decade, the commission ruled in the woman’s favour, holding the bank deficient in service. It directed the bank to refund the amount she had lost in the fraudulent transaction dated July 9, 2016.The bank has been ordered to pay the woman Rs 70,084, along with interest at 7% from the date of the transaction until the amount is paid. The bank must also pay her Rs 20,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.Two factors proved crucial to the woman’s case: reporting the unauthorised transactions promptly and supporting her complaint with documentary evidence.Anuj Dave, Practice Head (Ahmedabad & Mumbai) at Clavius Legal, told ET that the woman had informed the bank about the disputed transactions. She had also filed a police complaint and submitted documentary evidence in support of her case.The bank, meanwhile, alleged that the customer’s banking credentials had been compromised but failed to produce documentary evidence to establish negligence on her part.“The fundamental legal principle is that a bank cannot escape liability merely by alleging that an OTP or banking credentials were compromised. Under the RBI’s customer-protection framework relied upon in the order, the burden of establishing customer liability rests on the bank,” Dave said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic post-IPO hype is here. One strategist's advice: 'Stick to your fundamentals.'
articles.summary: A helpful quick guide on how to think through whether to invest in Anthropic post IPO.
articles.body:
Stick to your investing discipline as the post-IPO hype begins for newly minted public company Anthropic ( ANT ).

"I do think this name is very hyped. Whether that's deserved or not is definitely debatable," Renaissance Capital director of investment strategies Avery Marquez said on Sozzi Unleashed . "But don't go into it just with FOMO [fear of missing out] or hype. You really need to take a measured approach and stick to your fundamentals."

Shares of the AI model builder dropped in early trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.

But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains and closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day. That closing price gave Anthropic a market capitalization of about $1.28 trillion, or roughly $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Anthropic stock begins trading at $111.50 per share in record offering

Anthropic stock's first trade was worth $12 billion — 34% above its IPO price

How does Anthropic make money? Inside the business of AI.

To Marquez's point, there may be a near-term information vacuum about Anthropic, set against ongoing hype. For one, Wall Street analyst coverage of Anthropic won't begin for a few weeks. And two, the company's first earnings report as a public company is months away.

That leaves Anthropic's interesting S-1 as the continued source of fundamental truth on the company.

In a recent amended S-1 filing, Anthropic said that third quarter sales rose 1,127% to $17 billion. Revenue growth slowed on a quarter-over-quarter basis. Third quarter sales increased 47% compared with a 144% growth rate in the second quarter. Sales increased 132% in the first quarter.

The company also lost a staggering $23.29 billion in the third quarter.

articles.title: Behind Jensen Huang’s exit, questions about a management style reportedly built on fear
articles.summary: Elon Musk may have been overstating it when he said Nvidia’s employees “love” the ousted Jensen Huang.
articles.body:
Earlier this week at the DealBook conference in New York, Elon Musk, beamed in from a trip to China with President Donald Trump, was asked about the ouster of his longtime friend, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Musk compared it to kicking Michael Jordan off the Chicago Bulls' roster during his historic run. Of Nvidia's employees, he said, "They love [Huang]. They love him."

Well, maybe not all of them. Thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for Huang's return, but others tell The New York Times he ruled through praise and fear, as well as by humiliating people.

According to the Times, Huang told subordinates that Nvidia's wealth meant it wasn't possible to motivate employees with money, so humiliation was the only lever left. He reportedly told one executive his mother should have aborted him and told another employee he would rip his arms off and beat him to death with them.

Naturally, over a 33-year career, regrettable things may have been said, but the Times found a long paper trail that suggests the incidents weren't isolated. In 2005, for example, Michael Winston, a former HR chief, threatened to sue and called Huang's conduct the most abusive he'd seen. Nvidia paid him more than $1 million. Huang's spokesman calls the allegations fabrications.
